stem:
Meera reads in her school diary that a solar eclipse will be visible from her town next month. Her younger brother Aarav asks her how a solar eclipse happens.

Which explanation should Meera give?

options.text: The Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth and blocks sunlight from reaching a small area of the Earth.
The Moon is always bigger than the Sun, so it can easily cover the whole Sun.
A solar eclipse happens whenever the Moon is on the day side of the Earth, even if its shadow does not fall on the Earth.
The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon, so the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

teacher.key_rationale: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and the Earth and its shadow falls on a small region of the Earth; the Moon and Sun have similar apparent sizes as seen from Earth, so the Moon can block the Sun despite being physically smaller. Option B is the apparent/physical size confusion, C omits the shadow-reaching-Earth condition, and D conflates solar with lunar eclipse mechanics.
